text: 1 medium eggplant, cut into cubes 2 tablespoons finely chopped garlic 1 tablespoon chopped fresh parsley, chopped 2 ounces parmigiano-reggiano cheese 1 quart of white wine 1 lemon (may be substituted) Preheat oven to 375 degrees. Brown bacon in large skillet. Add onion and cook for 2 minutes. Add eggplant, season with salt and pepper and cook until tender, about 4 minutes. Remove from heat and cool. When cool, add bread, garlic, and bacon to eggplant and stir until well mixed. Add the parsley and cheese and mix well. Preheat broiler. Season trout with salt and pepper. Place on foil and reheat until warmed through. Then stuff the cavity with the eggplant mixture, add the wine, and fold foil over to seal, making a packet. Cook under broiler for about 25 minutes, or until fillets are flaky. Squeeze lemon juice over trout and serve on a large platter. Drizzle with olive oil and garnish with fresh parsley.

text: Deep convolutional networks have reached state-of-the-art performance in many medical image segmentation tasks. However, to generalize from one domain (e.g., one modality) to another, a domain adaptation step is required. In general, supervised domain adaptation yields the best results, but it requires a large amount of labeled data, which is often not available in practice. On the other hand, unsupervised methods require no new labeled data, but are usually unstable and hard to train. In this work, we propose a novel weakly supervised method. Instead of the detailed and time-consuming annotations, we just annotate a few examples from the target domain. This method is very easy to train because we add a regularization term to our loss function. Our method is evaluated on a case study of vestibular schwannoma (T1 to T2 MR images). Our proposed method outperforms unsupervised methods and achieves comparable results to a supervised method.
